newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Inespal to evaluate effects of strike Fri.
newsitem.headline: Spain Inespal to evaluate effects of strike Fri.

text.p: Spanish aluminium firm Inespal said on Thursday it would evaluate the effect of a strike in its factories on Friday.
"We will evaluate (any) effects of the strike on production tomorrow" a spokeswoman for the alumunium group said.
She said workers at five plants were not striking, but union pickets were impeding worker's entry at three others.
Workers are protesting at plans to sell the firm, unions said.
A source at Inespal's 83,000 tonne per year Aviles plant in Asturias said production there had not been stopped by a 24-hour strike which started at 0400 GMT.
"There's no stoppage, despite the strike. Potlines are still going. You can't stop the potlines process," he said.
"There are rumours that they'll call a strike every Thursday in all the Inespal plants, but no-one knows if this is true," he added.
Earlier, trades unions representing workers at Inespal said that 4,587 workers had gone on strike, and another stoppage had been called for July 10.
Local media reported that unions have called 24 hour strikes on July 17 and 24 as well.
